rows.question: What is the exposure dial's rule?
rows.answer: Morning, sir. The dial is simple: buying is allowed only when Bitcoin closes above both its 50-day average and its 200-day average. Otherwise no new buys, and cash is the position. Right now it's closed: Bitcoin closed at about 77,600, above its 200-day (about 73,200) but under its 50-day (about 80,500). Want me to show what the dial lets us do while it's closed?

rows.question: Which daily rule has a measured edge, and in which market state?
rows.answer: Morning, sir. Only one daily rule has a measured edge: the short dip trade, on tier-A coins, while the exposure dial is closed. It's closed right now. Bitcoin is under its 50-day average and above its 200-day. After costs the dip trade made about five percent a trade over random in both periods (review #26), and a point-in-time re-check on dead coins and live costs held up. Everything else has no measured edge, including every setup and every dial-open case. Want the details?

rows.question: How many coins do you watch live across the market?
rows.answer: Morning, sir. I watch about 393 coins live, all of them on Binance against USDT, and every rule runs on every coin. The 10 lab coins (Bitcoin, Ethereum, Solana, Cardano, Dogecoin, Avalanche, Bitcoin Cash, Chainlink, Litecoin, XRP) also get the 15-minute Explorer, and the rest are sorted by size. Want me to show the breakdown by tier?

rows.question: What did review 27 find about stops on dip buys?
need: no stop|without a stop|time exit|exit by time|time only
rows.answer: Morning, sir. Review 27 found that dip buys do best with no stop at all. In the 120-coin test, the short dip trade (H07) with no stop and a 10-day exit made about 6.5% a trade in 2018-2023 and 2.4% in 2024-2026. A tight stop made only about 0.5% and 0.4% in the same periods. A plain 200-day touch lost money with every exit tried. So the stop gets hit on the normal wobble and cuts off the bounce that pays. Want me to pull up the full review?

rows.question: What is the benchmark every strategy must beat?
rows.answer: Morning, sir. The benchmark is GATE50: hold Bitcoin only while it closes above its 50-day average, and sit in cash otherwise. Every strategy has to beat that after costs, and also beat a random entry with the same holding time. The dial we actually use is stricter. It needs Bitcoin above both its 50-day and 200-day averages. It beat the 50-day gate and plain holding in both test periods in review #25. Right now Bitcoin is under its 50-day, so both the benchmark and the dial say cash. Want the current scoreboard against it? Just say yes.

rows.question: Did tuning the deep-dip buy E6 in review 24 work?
rows.answer: Morning, sir. No, it didn't work. Review 24 found that none of the E6 deep-dip variants passes: every one loses money after costs in both test periods, and none beats random entries.

rows.question: What fee per side do we assume on NDAX?
rows.answer: Morning, sir. We assume 0.20% per side on NDAX, plus the measured spread. For coins outside the lab 10, we assume 0.40% for the spread.

rows.question: How much of the book does one setup trade risk in the 500 dollar book?
rows.answer: Morning, sir. In the $500 book, each setup trade risks 0.5% of the book, so about two and a half dollars if the stop is hit. One trade can't be more than 10% of the book, about fifty dollars, and total risk across all open trades is capped at 6%, about thirty dollars.

rows.question: What daily loss stops new buys in the 500 dollar book?
rows.answer: Morning, sir. A 2% fall in the book in one day stops new buys. The weekly brake is 4%, and four losses in a row or a 15% fall from the peak pauses the book until you resume it. The day brake has fired twice, on Oct 22 and Oct 28, and Oct 28 also set off the weekly brake. That block runs to about Nov 2. The book is down about 10.7% since Oct 11, at roughly 447 Canadian dollars. All four closed trades lost, and graduation is 3 of 10 gates, not ready. Want the brake log in full?

rows.question: What happens if the 500 dollar book falls 15% from its peak?
rows.answer: Morning, sir. If the $500 book falls 15% from its peak, it pauses all trading and stays paused until you resume it. It won't restart on its own. That's the last of its four brakes. The other three are timed: 2% in a day, 4% in a week, and 4 losses in a row. The book is worth about 447 Canadian dollars, down about 11% from the 500 start. That's below the 15% line, but I can't see the peak figure the brake measures from. The 15% brake has never fired. The week brake did on Oct 28 and it runs until Nov 2, so the book is already paused by that one. Want me to walk through how it resumes after a pa

rows.question: How many losing trades in a row pause buying?
rows.answer: Morning, sir. Four losses in a row pause buying. That's one of the brakes on the $500 NDAX book: 2% in a day, 4% in a week, 4 losses in a row, or a 15% fall from the peak. Once one fires, buying stays paused until you resume it. Want me to check whether any brake has fired?

rows.question: What does the core sleeve of the 500 dollar book hold?
rows.answer:
Good morning, sir. The core sleeve holds nothing right now. It's all cash.

The dial is closed, meaning Bitcoin is under its 50-day or 200-day average, so the core plan is "no core: cash". The core's last positions, Bitcoin and Ethereum, were sold on Oct 29 and 30. Ethereum went on a close under its own 50-day average. Bitcoin went because the dial closed.

The core has lost money on all four of its closed trades. The book is about 447 Canadian dollars, down about 10.7%. Of that, about 403 is cash and the rest sits in two short dip trades (Avalanche and Solana) in the edge sleeve. Those aren't

rows.question: Which exchange is the 500 dollar book built for?
rows.answer: Morning, sir. The $500 book is built for NDAX, in Canadian dollars. Every paper fill is checked to sit inside NDAX's bid and ask, and costs use NDAX's 0.20% fee plus spread. It's paper only, with no exchange connected.

rows.question: How many trigger points does an Explorer setup give the brain now?
rows.answer: Morning, sir. An Explorer setup gives the brain zero trigger points now. The repair shop's trigger-weights review changed it to follow the evidence, and the Explorer is retired as a trading book with no edge after costs. So it can't wake the brain on its own.

rows.question: What daily trading volume puts a coin in tier A?
rows.answer: Morning, sir. A coin is tier A when it trades over $20 million a day. Tier B is $1 million to $20 million, and tier C is under $1 million. Tier C coins are watched but never judged.

rows.question: What do you hold when the dial is closed?
rows.answer: Morning, sir. When the exposure dial is closed, cash is the position and we hold no main trades. The only exception is the short dip trade on tier-A coins, our single measured edge when the market gate is shut. Want to see how the trend portfolio is set up right now?

rows.question: What is the H07 entry?
rows.answer: Morning, sir. The H07 entry is the short dip trade. You buy a coin when its 10-day RSI, a gauge of how stretched the price is, closes under 30 on the daily candle while the coin is still above its 200-day average. You exit when RSI is back over 40, or after 10 days. There's no stop. It only counts in one measured cell: tier-A coins while the exposure dial is closed, and the dial is closed now. One caution: the status card says H07 was parked on Oct 29, so it's no longer a reason to buy.

rows.question: What is Madhav's M1 setup?
rows.answer: Morning, sir. Your M1 is the capitulation setup: a buy at the lows after a sharp sell-off where many holders give up at once, like your June 5 Solana buy. On its own, history from 2018 to 2023 did not support it as a buy signal (review #5), so when it shows I treat it as a place to look, not a reason to buy.

rows.question: How many coins are in the research lake?
rows.answer: Morning, sir. The research lake holds 120 coins, with checked history back to 2017, including coins that were delisted. They're for research only, so we don't watch or trade them. Of the 120, 30 are the paper tier and 10 are the live lab coins. Separately, we watch about 390 coins live on Binance. Want the tiers in more detail?

rows.question: Is the hourly watch running?
rows.answer: Morning, sir. No, the hourly watch is parked. You parked it on Oct 11 (decision D6) because it had only 2 setups in 12 days, and the code is kept. Its book, Hunter's book, is frozen at 22 trades with 3 wins and 19 losses, down about $32 with $967 left. Do you want me to confirm that nothing else is down?

rows.question: What will Bitcoin's price be on December 31, 2026?
rows.answer: Morning, sir. I can't tell you Bitcoin's price on December 31, and nobody honestly can. Bitcoin is at about 77 thousand 800 dollars, under its 50-day average of about 80 thousand 500 and above its 200-day average of about 73 thousand 200. The market is in a closed state, so we hold cash. If you want a lean, I'd expect chop between roughly 73 thousand and 80 thousand near term. A daily close under 73 thousand would change my mind and point lower.

rows.question: Will Ethereum beat Solana next month?
rows.answer: Morning, sir. I can't call that one, and I'd put it close to a coin flip. Over the past week Ethereum is down about two and a half percent and Solana about six, so Ethereum has held up better. Our own tests found strength against Bitcoin didn't work as a filter, so I wouldn't lean on that for a month-long call. Both fired the short dip trade at last night's close, with the market still closed to new buys, so neither is a buy for us right now. Want me to pull up the dip setups?

rows.question: What did review 40 find?
rows.answer:
Morning, sir. There's no review 40 yet. The brief says 30 reviews are done, 12 of them passed, and the review list I pulled stops at number 31, which is still pending.

The latest ones with results are #29 and #30, both passes:
- **#29:** the short dip trade holds up on the point-in-time tier A while the dial is closed. That's +10.4% then +6.8% a trade over random, after costs.
- **#30:** the trend portfolio still passes on the top 10 coins as they really were each month, but much weaker (+3.7% in 2024-26). Holding the same coins lost 31.9%.

The newer ones are forward tests that run on live d

rows.question: On what exact date will the next Bitcoin crash start?
rows.answer: Morning, sir. I can't give you a date, and nobody honestly can. Crashes aren't scheduled, and nothing we've tested predicts one to the day. What I can tell you is where the line sits: Bitcoin closed at about 77,600, under its 50-day average (80,500) but about six percent above its 200-day (73,200). The dial is closed, so we hold cash and buy nothing new. A daily close under about 73,200 would be the real warning, and my own view says I'd change my mind there.

rows.question: Which coin will rise the most tomorrow?
rows.answer: Morning, sir. I can't tell you which coin will rise most tomorrow, and nothing we've tested picks that. The market is closed to new buys: Bitcoin is under its 50-day average, so cash is our position. If I had to lean, I'd watch Avalanche, which is up about two and a half percent today and is one of the coins closest to a short dip entry. That's a guess, not a signal.

rows.question: What win rate did the E9 setup have in 2019?
rows.answer:
Good morning, sir. I can't give you a 2019 win rate for E9, because I have no setup called E9. The Explorer's setups run E1 to E6. E7 and E8 are dip setups we only watch and never trade. I searched our research and found nothing under that name.

You may mean one of two things. The Explorer's setups were tested against history in the atlas, which runs 2017 to 2026. The short dip trade (H07) was tested over 2018 to 2023, and it won about 70% of its trades. That's a six-year window, not 2019 alone. Which one did you mean?

rows.question: What did our backtest on 3-minute candles show?
rows.answer: Morning, sir. We never ran a backtest on 3-minute candles, and I found no record of one. Our shortest history is 5-minute candles, and the Explorer works on 15-minute bars. The short-timeframe tests we did run all failed after costs. The green-run study on 5-minute candles had none of its 67,167 cells pass. Review #24 on 15-minute dips lost after costs in both periods. I'd expect 3-minute bars to do worse, since costs would take a bigger share of each tiny move. That's my reasoning, not a test result. Want me to flag a 3-minute test for the repair shop?

rows.question: Will the dial be open on New Year's Day?
rows.answer: Morning, sir. I can't tell you that. New Year's Day is about two months away, and the dial only reads where Bitcoin sits against its 50-day and 200-day averages today. Right now it's closed: the brief shows the Bitcoin gate shut, so the trend portfolio is all cash and no new buys are allowed.

rows.question: What is the guaranteed profit of an H07 trade next week?
rows.answer: Morning, sir. There's no guaranteed profit on the short dip trade, or on anything we run. It's paper money, and the evidence behind it is thin. The one measured edge was about five percent a trade over random after costs, but only on big coins while the Bitcoin rule is closed. That's an average over many trades, not a promise for next week. The Bitcoin gate is closed right now, and the dip trade was parked on Oct 29 as a reason to buy.

rows.question: What did our review of Cardano staking rewards find?
rows.answer: Morning, sir. We have no review of Cardano staking rewards. I searched our research and found nothing on staking for Cardano or any other coin. Staking yield isn't something Ananta records or tests, because our reviews cover price-based setups, the trend portfolio, the dip trade and zones. Want me to flag it as an idea for the repair shop? Just say yes.

rows.question: Why is the exposure dial open or closed right now?
rows.answer: Morning, sir. The dial is closed, so no new buys and cash is the position. Bitcoin closed Friday at about 77,600, under its 50-day average of about 80,500, and the dial needs it above both the 50-day and the 200-day. It's still above the 200-day, at about 73,200. Bitcoin is at about 77,800 now, so it needs roughly 3.5% more to reopen the dial. Since Oct 10 the dial's paper book is down 7.9%, against 6.5% for just holding, so it hasn't beaten holding yet and the evidence is thin.

rows.question: Why do we buy the H07 dip only when the dial is closed?
rows.answer: Morning, sir. We buy it only when the dial is closed because that's the one place history showed an edge. In review #26, tier-A coins bought on a dip while Bitcoin was below its 50-day and 200-day averages beat random by about 5 percent a trade after costs, in both test periods. With the dial open, or on smaller coins, there's no measured edge. One more thing: the card says H07 was parked on Oct 29, so it's no longer a reason to buy right now.

rows.question: Why does the 500 dollar book sit in cash when the dial is closed?
rows.answer: Morning, sir. The $500 book sits in cash because the exposure dial is closed. The dial is closed when Bitcoin is below its 50-day or 200-day average, and the brief shows the Bitcoin gate is shut. In that state we have no tested edge on the core coins, so cash is the position. The core, Bitcoin 40% and Ethereum 20%, only gets bought when the dial opens. The one exception is the edge sleeve, the short dip trade on big coins, which was measured to work while the dial is closed. But that trade was parked on Oct 29 and is no longer a reason to buy. So I haven't confirmed what the book holds right n

rows.question: Why does the 500 dollar book stop buying after four losing trades in a row?
rows.answer: Morning, sir. It stops because four straight losses is where I can't tell bad luck from a broken rule, so buying pauses until you resume it. That number is a safety limit you set, not something we measured. Right now the losing-streak brake hasn't fired and its counter is zero. The day-loss brake fired twice and the week-loss brake once, and buying is blocked until about Nov 2. Want me to go through what each brake blocked?

rows.question: Why do the dip buys have no stop loss?
rows.answer: Morning, sir. The dip buys have no stop because testing showed a stop made them worse. With no stop and a 10-day exit, the short dip trade earned about 6.5% and 2.4% a trade in the two test periods. With a tight stop it earned only about half a percent and 0.4%. Dips usually bounce back, and a tight stop sells you out right before the bounce.

rows.question: Can we buy today? Answer yes or no first, then why.
rows.answer: Morning, sir. No, we can't buy today. The exposure dial is closed: Bitcoin is under its 50-day average at about 80 thousand 5 hundred, though still above its 200-day at about 73 thousand. The one exception is the short dip trade on big coins, and ETH and SOL fired it on last night's close. That trade is still thin evidence, and it was parked on Oct 29 as a reason to buy.
rows.answer2: Morning, sir. No, not for normal buys today. The exposure dial is CLOSED: Bitcoin closed at about 77,600, under its 50-day average of about 80,500, so cash is the position. The one exception is the short dip trade, which fired on Ethereum and Solana at last night's close. It's the only measured edge while the dial is closed, but it sits in the book 500 rules, and the thin evidence is worth remembering.

rows.question: In one or two sentences, what is your view of the market right now?
rows.answer: Morning, sir. My view is defensive: the market is closed to new buys, and cash is the position. Bitcoin is about 77,800, under its 50-day average (80,500) but still above its 200-day (73,200), so I expect more chop near the lows. The one live idea is the short dip trade on ETH and SOL, which fired at last night's close.
rows.answer2: Morning, sir. My view is still defensive. The dial is closed because Bitcoin, at about 77.8 thousand, sits under its 50-day average of about 80.5 thousand, so no new buys and cash is the position. It's quiet chop near the lows, and Bitcoin only turns worse for the short dip trade if it closes under about 73.2 thousand, its 200-day average.
